note: Joining three Dorian positions with one word for the way across, "the crossing": position 1 to 2 and position 2 to 3 on position-necks with cross, then phrases across all three over a drone. The old Key choice is now moves (any key), named only as {{=key}}, so the last block is a new task in place of the same crossing in other keys; each position is named with its scale the first time, and the {{?key}} line says what stays the same.

exercise.title: Join the Dorian positions
exercise.why: Each position starts on the notes where the one below ends, so one move along one string carries a line from one position into the next.

cells.text:
The neck below shows only the crossing from position 1 to position 2 of the {{=key}} Dorian scale: position 1 on the low strings, position 2 on the high strings. Start on the ringed {{1}} on the low E string and climb position 1. On the G string, move up into position 2 as the dots show, and finish the climb there.
Come back down the same way, crossing back on the G string.
Practice until your hand moves at the crossing without you stopping to look.

The neck below shows the crossing one position higher, from position 2 to position 3 of {{=key}} Dorian. Climb position 2, cross on the G string, and finish in position 3.
Then play both crossings in a row, from the low {{1}} in position 1 up to the top of position 3, and back down.

Press Play below to start the drone on {{=key}}. Under it are positions 1, 2 and 3 of {{=key}} Dorian. Make up short phrases that use a crossing to move into the next position, and end each one on a ringed {{1}}.
{{?key}}In another key the positions sit on other frets, and each crossing is still on the G string.
